title: Rock Labyrinths
lead: The only plate mountains in Poland. Błędne Skały, Szczeliniec Wielki, and rock formations that look like sculptures.
body:
The Only Plate Mountains in Poland

Table Mountains National Park is the only park in Poland that protects plate mountains — a unique type of mountain where instead of sharp peaks there are vast plateaus and fanciful rock formations. The Table Mountains were formed from sandstone deposited on the seabed over 100 million years ago, then uplifted and shaped by erosion.

The most famous place in the park is Szczeliniec Wielki (919 m) — the highest peak of the Table Mountains, reached by over 600 steps. From the summit, a panorama opens up over the Sudetes, the Kłodzko Valley, and the surrounding towns.

Błędne Skały and Labyrinths

The second icon of the park is Błędne Skały — a labyrinth of crevices, corridors, and rock chambers where you can get lost for hours. The rock formations have various shapes — from mushrooms and towers to figures and animals. It is worth walking the entire route, stopping at the most interesting formations.

The park offers many trails — from easy walks to demanding hikes. It is also worth paying attention to the Road of a Hundred Bends — a scenic car route that leads through the most interesting corners of the park and offers spectacular views.
tip: Go to Błędne Skały early in the morning, before the crowds. The labyrinth is then quiet and mysterious, and the narrow crevices look most magical.
